classification_legend.A: Existing engine/mechanical/contact evidence is sufficient; no new user reference is required.
classification_legend.B: A still-image posture target is needed; timing can be authored by the contract and solver.
classification_legend.C: A native-speed video is needed for timing, momentum, force-chain, or contact order.
classification_legend.D: Both a posture still and a native-speed video are needed.
classification_legend.E: Do not visually imitate an assumed animal performance; use a provenance-labeled bounded gameplay/engineering reconstruction.

capture_protocol.native_speed_definition: Capture and encode the performance at its intended playback rate; do not retime slow motion into contract timing.
capture_protocol.paired_camera_rule: Side and three-quarter takes use the same scale, lens, floor, target placement, and timing. Front/rear or top views are requested only where lateral support or target/terrain relation matters.
capture_protocol.provenance_rule: Requested captures must be original project-owned or properly commissioned. Their fps recommendations are engineering capture choices, not biological claims.

animations.phase_summary: Target lock → posture elevation → body alignment → sustained vigilance → loop settle.
animations.rationale: Historical alert-idle and alert posture intent cover the needed static silhouette and support behavior; do not request a duplicate still.

animations.phase_summary: Alternating contact/load/toe-off/swing cycle with root motion and head stabilization.

animations.phase_summary: Interrupt → acoustic recognition → processing freeze → lower-body preparation → alert handoff.

animations.phase_summary: Standing assessment → foot reposition → lowering → first ground support → pelvis/torso settle → head/neck settle.

animations.phase_summary: Supported rest → deep breath → rare head adjustment → relaxation drift → breath/loop close.
